items.body: `check_registered` always returns `Reject` for an empty path. The unchanged `Runtime::reach` first calls `reach_evidence(observation, &[])` and immediately abandons exploration when that returns `Reject`. Consequently, consumers delegating to this registry—as the synthetic binding does—cannot explain any `Projection::Reach` observation. The tests supply prebuilt nonempty paths and bypass this admission step.
items.suggestion: Provide explicit root admission for supported evidence, returning an appropriate continuation cursor. Add a synthetic test exercising the registry through `Runtime` with `Projection::Reach`.
items.title: `check_registered` always returns `Reject` for an empty path

items.body: Newly accepted opaque metadata still reaches the existing whole-module semantic scanner. For example, `#[metadata(example(reject!(NotFound)))]` sets `Machine.rejecting` because `declare::machine` recursively searches all tokens for `reject!`. This changes the generated outcome type from `()` to `umpire_dsl::Outcome`, its catalog, and transition expansion despite unchanged handlers. Metadata therefore affects Model semantics and can break callers requiring `Outcome = ()`.
items.suggestion: Exclude metadata payloads from semantic macro detection, or inspect executable bodies. Add a regression proving opaque `reject!` and `stay!` tokens preserve native and lifted semantics.
items.title: Newly accepted opaque metadata still reaches the existing whole-module semantic scanner
